column2: Which entry on a travel insurance application is special category data under UK GDPR?
column6: Details of a motoring conviction
column7: Health information receives special category protection. Criminal convictions are covered by a separate provision.

column2: Which use of biometric data by an insurer brings it within the special category for biometrics?
column3: Matching a voiceprint to identify a caller
column4: Recording a call for training purposes
column5: Storing a portrait on a staff profile
column6: Photographing the scene of an accident
column7: The special category covers biometric data used to identify a person uniquely. An ordinary recording or photograph does not by itself meet that test.

column2: A broker removes irrelevant questions from its quotation form. Which UK GDPR principle does this apply?
column6: Accuracy
column7: Restricting what a firm collects to what it needs implements data minimisation. Storage limitation concerns how long it keeps identifiable records.

column2: Which measure demonstrates accountability for a claims department's handling of personal data?
column3: Documenting its checks against the principles
column4: Correcting a policyholder's date of birth
column5: Restricting access to the claims archive
column6: Deleting records at the end of retention
column7: The accountability principle requires the controller to be able to demonstrate compliance. A correction implements accuracy and a retention period implements storage limitation.

column2: A proposer discloses a previous prison sentence. Which classification applies under UK GDPR?
column6: Anonymous statistical information
column7: Article 10 governs personal information about offences and convictions. A conviction remains identifiable personal data when attached to a named applicant.

column2: What determines how long an insurer should keep a closed claim file in identifiable form?
column4: When the next insurer audit falls due
column5: The date the policy was first issued
column6: The length of the original period of cover
column7: Retention follows the need for the information, including any applicable legal obligations. The original term of cover alone does not set a retention period.

column2: A life policy designates an individual recipient. What must the insurer record at that stage?
column4: A certified copy of their will
column5: A statement of their net assets
column6: A declaration of their tax residence
column7: For a named beneficiary, the money laundering regulations require the insurer to take the full name when the person is designated. Verification has a separate deadline.

column2: Which source meets the independence requirement when verifying a life policy customer's identity?
column3: A passport issued by the state
column4: A proposal written by the applicant
column5: A declaration signed by the customer
column6: A personal summary of address changes
column7: An official identity document is independent evidence even when the customer hands it to the insurer. Repeating an applicant's own assertions adds no independent confirmation.

column2: A life policy benefits a class of future grandchildren. What information should the insurer obtain at designation?
column3: Details sufficient to identify them at payout
column4: The amounts each grandchild will inherit
column5: Individual tax returns for the policyholder
column6: Valuations of assets in the wider estate
column7: For beneficiaries described by class, the insurer must have sufficient information to establish who qualifies when the policy pays out. It need not know the identity of unborn beneficiaries.

column2: When must a life insurer complete identity verification of a designated beneficiary at the latest?
column6: At the next review of the sum insured
column7: A beneficiary's identity must be verified before payment under the policy. Recording a name on designation is a separate step.

column2: A life insurer proposes a business relationship with a politically exposed person. Whose approval is required?
column6: The introducing intermediary
column7: The regulations place the approval with senior management. This accompanies checks on wealth and funds and enhanced monitoring.

column2: Which enquiry establishes the source of funds for a particular life insurance premium?
column4: How the customer accumulated their fortune
column5: Who may receive the maturity payment
column6: Which intermediary arranged the contract
column7: Source of funds concerns money used for the transaction. Source of wealth concerns how the person's wider assets were acquired.

column2: A complaint is resolved the day after receipt. Which written notice must the insurance firm promptly send?
column5: A statement of demands and needs
column6: A written acknowledgement of receipt
column7: The early-resolution procedure requires written confirmation of resolution and information about the ombudsman. An acknowledgement alone confirms receipt.

column2: Several complaints reveal a calculation error in one product. What wider check does DISP require?
column3: Whether the cause affects other products
column4: Whether redress was paid in each case
column6: Whether the response deadline was met
column7: Firms must consider whether a recurring cause also affects other products or processes. Meeting a response target does not identify the wider impact of a faulty calculation.

column2: An insurer rejects a complaint in its final response after three weeks. When may the consumer contact FOS?
column6: When the six-month period expires
column7: A dissatisfied consumer can refer the case on receiving the final response. The eight-week rule allows referral when an ordinary insurance complaint has gone unanswered.

column2: What is the normal deadline for referring an insurance complaint after the firm's final response?
column3: Six months from the date on the response
column4: Eight weeks from the date of the loss
column5: Three months from the date cover ended
column6: One year from the initial complaint
column7: The usual referral window runs from the date of the final response. The time the firm had to investigate the complaint is a different period.

column2: Whom does an ombudsman's final determination bind if the complainant accepts it within the deadline?
column6: Every firm in that insurance class
column7: Timely acceptance makes the final determination binding on both parties. The decision resolves their dispute.

column2: An insurer fails today. Which eligible claim attracts full FSCS insurance protection?
column6: Private bicycle theft claim
column7: Professional indemnity is among the classes protected at 100%. Most ordinary property policies are protected at 90%.

column2: An insurer fails today owing an eligible £4,000 household contents theft claim. What would FSCS normally pay?
column7: Ordinary household contents insurance attracts 90% protection. Multiplying £4,000 by 0.90 gives £3,600.

column2: What funds FSCS protection for eligible policyholders when an authorised insurer fails?
column6: Tax deducted from insurance settlements
column7: FSCS is funded by industry levies. A policy excess is the portion of a loss borne under the policy.

column2: A CII member faces conflicting core duties. Which one takes priority under the Code?
column3: Complying with applicable law and the Code
column4: Acting in the interests of each client
column5: Providing a high standard of service
column6: Treating people fairly across protected groups
column7: The Code gives its compliance duty priority when it conflicts with another core duty. Client interests remain central within that boundary.

column2: Whom does the Code expressly identify as the recipient of a report about a breach of the Code?
column6: Financial Services Compensation Scheme
column7: The professional Code requires breaches to be reported to the CII. Regulatory notifications and individual complaints have their own routes.

column2: A broker advertises fee-free advice but charges an arrangement fee. Which service obligation is directly at issue?
column6: Procedure for handling complaints
column7: The Code's service standard requires members to be open about fees and other costs. Recording the charge internally would not correct the client's impression.

column2: Which CII duty applies most directly when a broker challenges age-based assumptions about claimants?
column6: Disclosing the cost of advice
column7: The fair-treatment duty covers age and calls for individual treatment. A claimant's age alone does not establish what help they need.

column2: Two business partners ask a broker to advise them separately. Which relationship creates a professional conflict?
column3: Competing duties on the same transaction
column5: Joint instructions on the same acquisition
column6: Separate premiums on a shared policy
column7: Under the Code, a conflict can arise when an adviser owes competing duties to different clients. Having a business connection alone is insufficient.

column2: A claims supervisor assigns a trainee unfamiliar work. Which obligation specifically concerns the supervisor's staff?
column4: Keeping clients informed after a sale
column5: Explaining the basis of a claims settlement
column6: Describing the level of cover accurately
column7: The service standard makes the development and oversight of staff a responsibility of those managing them.

column2: An intermediary promises a policy benefit the contract excludes. Which client-interest provision has been breached?
column6: Restricting personal use of work information
column7: The CII Code requires promises about product performance and after-sales service to be true. An unsupported promise misstates what the policy delivers.

column2: A CII member's conduct outside work damages the profession's reputation. Which core duty covers this?
column6: Treating colleagues and customers fairly
column7: The integrity duty covers conduct inside and outside work that brings the profession or the CII into disrepute. It can apply without an advisory relationship.
